tasks.task: Build a 13-week cash forecast and flag the tight weeks

items.when: When you have a bank export, unpaid invoices, bills and pay dates and need a weekly view
When the owner wants a quick 30, 60 and 90 day view with the risks named
When income is seasonal, to get a dated forecast, a downside case and actions
When you need the worst case in plain words: three bad-year tests and the breaking point
When last period's forecast can be set against what happened, to see each miss and why
When the forecast has no slack, to ask how much room for error the business needs

tasks.task: Explain budget versus actual with causes

items.when: When a number moved against budget, forecast or last period and the owner asks why
When you have actual and budget figures and need what moved, why, and a short note
When one department overspent, to get a reconciled report and options for its owner
Each month, to track what moved against budget and the cash levers if the year is off

tasks.task: Build a 12-month budget for the business or a team

items.when: Two to three months before the year starts, or after a big change, to run the whole cycle
When you have last year's monthly numbers and next year's goals
When the budget should run from named drivers, with an inputs sheet and cash
When each department needs a phased budget from its past spend and targets
When you want a second budget built from the same history to compare with yours
When pay is the largest cost, to budget it by team and month from the headcount plan
When the budget is drafted, to see where it breaks in a bad year and how to fix it

tasks.task: Build plan, cautious and stretch versions

items.when: When three versions should run from one set of drivers, so they stay comparable
When hiring is the big swing, to get base, best and worst cases and switch signals
When the cautious case looks mild, to test the plan against three bad years
When the versions are built, to recalculate them and see which assumptions matter most
When the worst case is only a little worse, to look for the shock that ends the business

tasks.task: Update the full-year forecast after month end

items.when: Once the month is closed, and each Monday for the cash refresh
When a model exists and new results are in, to update it and flag the biggest changes
When sales have seasons and spikes, to find the trend and a forecast table
Before the new forecast goes out, to see how far the last one missed

tasks.task: Write the one-page monthly numbers review

items.when: At month end, when the owner wants five numbers, how they moved and what to do
Before the page, to pick the few numbers that match the decisions the reader makes
When the review should also run weekly with a forecast and a dashboard
When one number needs a clean chart drawn from the client's own data
When the page is a slide, to check every number and chart agrees with the workbook
When the page is crowded, to keep one message per chart and put the action in view

tasks.task: Build a three-year financial model

items.when: When a young company needs revenue, costs, hires, cash and runway from named drivers
When you want a second build from the same numbers to compare structure and results
When the model must also give a cash-out date with ranges and a finance pack
When every assumption needs logging with its risk on one page
Before anyone relies on it, to find formula errors, broken links and totals that do not tie
When the numbers and the story have drifted apart, to make each assumption follow the story

tasks.task: Show assumptions, sources and which inputs matter most

items.when: When a reader must see every assumption and how it could change the answer
When one input needs a low, base and high value with its reasoning listed
When you need the model re-run to rank which assumptions move the result most
When the inputs sheet must let a non-finance partner change a driver and see the effect

tasks.task: Turn subscription data into trusted recurring revenue metrics

items.when: When you have a billing export and need revenue movement, churn and retention you can trust
When the numbers are worked out, to read them and see what to fix first
When subscriptions run through a store, to get recurring revenue, subscribers and churn
When the founder wants the same sheet kept each week with one growth target
When churn must be watched between reports so a rise is caught early

tasks.task: Analyse churn and retention by customer group

items.when: When churn must be split by plan, start month or size, with failed payments told apart
When you have activity data, to get retention curves by sign-up group
When the reader needs retention by group as a colour grid with a plain reading
When one group looks worse, to keep watching it month to month

tasks.task: Check cost to win a customer, payback and lifetime value

items.when: When money is spent to win customers and the owner asks how fast it comes back
When you have customer and revenue data, to work out cohorts, payback and value
When the figures are in, to get profit against cost to win and a scale-or-fix call

tasks.task: Break a sales or margin change into price, volume and mix

items.when: When revenue or margin moved between two periods and you need each part sized
When the bridge needs causes beside each part, not only amounts
When the change is in making cost, to split it into price, volume and efficiency
When the bridge should be shown as a waterfall chart from the worked numbers
When the parts do not add back to the total, to rework the sum a second way

tasks.task: Find why sales dipped or spiked

items.when: When online sales fell, to split the drop into visits, conversion and order value
When you have before and after numbers, to find the lever that moved and the next check
When the move may be seasonal, to test it against trend and past seasons
When the cause is found and must be written up with amounts

tasks.task: Show which products or jobs moved the margin

items.when: When you have revenue and costs by product, to see each margin and the loss-makers
When the business sells hours, to turn paid hours into revenue and delivery margin
When shared costs must be split across products or sites by how much each used
When margins are known, to find break-even volume and the effect of a price change
When the margin change must be split into price, volume and mix

tasks.task: Review fixed costs from zero

items.when: Once a year, or when profit or cash is under pressure, to question every fixed cost
When subscriptions have piled up, to get a register and savings scenarios
When you have a list of supplier payments, to group spend and rank the savings

tasks.task: Build a business case for a purchase or hire

items.when: When the owner asks whether to buy, to work out payback, return and risk
When the purchase replaces a vehicle, to compare the cash both ways
When the spend is a hire, to show full yearly cost, hire against contractor and payback
When there are several ways to do it, to see options, cash impact and a downside case
When the saving comes from a supplier's own figures, to test the claim
When the case is made, to show what the payments do to cash week by week

tasks.task: Work out ways to close a cash gap

items.when: First, to size the gap and name the weeks it falls in
When cash may be stuck in debtors, creditors or stock, to see where and how much
When several projects compete for the same cash, to compare which fit the limit
When stretching supplier terms is one option, to see the float and what to ask for
When the owner must choose, to set out the options with cash impact and downside

tasks.task: Write a one-page guide to update the forecast each week

items.when: When the forecast is built and the owner must keep it going without you
When the workbook needs its inputs, formulas, update steps and risks written down
Before handover, to find broken formulas and totals that do not add up

tasks.task: Plan hiring and what it will cost

items.when: When you have headcount history and goals and need a role-by-role plan with monthly cost
When the plan is set and must become a budget by team and month
When hiring depends on sales, to compare base, best and worst cases
When the hires must tie into the main model's profit, cash and runway

tasks.task: Forecast startup burn and runway

items.when: When you have monthly cash data and need the burn and the month cash runs out
When the board or investors need the cash-out date with ranges and a plan
When runway must respond to hires and revenue drivers, not a flat burn
When runway rests on sales arriving on time, to test it against a bad year

tasks.task: Prepare a board, investor or lender numbers pack

items.when: When decisions are due, to map the evidence and write the update around them
When the quarter must become a deck outline with the numbers and bad news placed right
When a lender tests cash cover, to show the cushion in each test period
When profit looks fine, to set free cash beside it before a lender does
Before the meeting, to face the toughest questions and drill the numbers
Before sending, to check each slide number and chart against the workbook

tasks.task: Work out break-even and the effect of a price change

items.when: When you have prices and costs and need break-even volume and margin of safety
When a new price is on the table, to see three outcome cases and a test you can undo
When the price change alters what a customer is worth against the cost to win one

tasks.task: Review a budget or model someone else built

items.when: First, to find formula errors, broken links and statements that do not tie
When figures must be recalculated and the weak assumptions named
When the sums are right, to test whether the plan survives a bad year
When the model can be set against actuals to see where it has already missed

always.when: Before any workbook leaves you, to find broken formulas and totals that do not add up
Whenever a number rests on a guess, to log the guess and its risk beside the result

helpers.when: When the actuals are not closed or reconciled and the numbers cannot yet be trusted
When the forecast shows a funding need or a decision that is bigger than the numbers
When the bridge or margin work points to a pricing problem that needs its own study
When the model is for a raise and needs an investor story and terms around it
When the pack needs several charts or a dashboard designed, not one chart
When exports need heavy cleaning or the workbook needs advanced formulas or macros

gaps: No library item builds a weekly 13-week direct cash forecast; the library forecast works in 30, 60 and 90 days
No library item builds a price, volume and mix bridge or checks that its parts add back to the total
No library item draws a waterfall chart of a change; only a general chart drawer exists
No library item builds a sensitivity table or ranks the three inputs that move a model most
No library item reviews fixed costs from zero, line by line
No library item builds a driver-based budget with plan, cautious and stretch versions in one spreadsheet layout
No library item compares buy, lease and finance for a machine, software or fit-out; only vehicles are covered
No library item writes a business case memo for an owner or a lender
No library item turns a Stripe, Paddle or Chargebee export into revenue movement, or tells real churn from failed payments
No library item offers two or three layouts of a one-page numbers review to compare
No library item forecasts working capital or plans capital spending for a small business
